meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: What a document shape permits that a table of columns cannot
questions.learningObjective: Identify a capability a document shape has over fixed columns
questions.stem: A planning tool stores each plan as one document with varying fields; what can it do that a fixed-column table cannot?

options.text: Store different attributes per plan without schema migrations
Guarantee every plan has identical fields
Prevent any field from being null
Make all queries use indexes automatically

questions.explanation: Documents allow heterogeneous fields without migrations. The belief that they enforce uniformity or auto-index is wrong.
questions.hint: Documents skip schema migrations for new fields.

questions.topic: The write cost an index adds
questions.learningObjective: State the write cost of maintaining an index
questions.stem: Every new index on the plans table slows which operation?

options.misconception: indexes help reads not slow them

options.text: Inserts, updates, and deletes, because each index must be maintained
Nothing; indexes are free on writes

questions.explanation: Each index adds work to writes. The belief that indexes are free or only affect reads is false.
questions.hint: Indexes cost work on every write.

questions.topic: Reading the three words a plan uses to describe its work
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a query plan's access and join operators
questions.stem: A plan says Seq Scan, Hash Join, Sort; what does Seq Scan imply?

options.text: The query uses a hash index
The relation is read row by row without an index

questions.explanation: Seq Scan means a full sequential read. Hash Join and Sort are separate operations.
questions.hint: Seq Scan is a full table read.

questions.topic: A server-sent event and the one direction it allows
questions.learningObjective: State the direction of a server-sent event stream
questions.stem: The planning board uses server-sent events for live updates; which way can data flow?

answer.exemplar: Data flows only from server to client over a single HTTP connection; the client cannot send data back on that same stream.

questions.explanation: SSE is unidirectional server to client. Bidirectional needs WebSockets or separate requests.
questions.hint: SSE is server to client only.

questions.topic: A socket that closes and the handshake that reopens it
questions.learningObjective: Describe the WebSocket handshake that reopens a closed socket
questions.stem: After a WebSocket closes, how does the client reopen it?

options.text: Resume the old TCP connection automatically
Send a ping frame and wait
options.misconception: ping does not reopen a closed socket

options.text: Perform a new HTTP upgrade handshake to establish a fresh socket

questions.explanation: Reopening requires a new upgrade handshake. Ping or stream reuse does not recreate a closed socket.
questions.hint: A new upgrade handshake is needed.

questions.topic: What actually delivers an ordering guarantee
questions.learningObjective: Identify what truly provides an ordering guarantee
questions.stem: The planning feed claims in-order delivery; what actually guarantees it?

options.misconception: TCP order is per connection not end to end

options.text: A single ordered channel or sequence numbers with reordering

questions.explanation: Ordering needs an ordered channel or explicit sequence handling. TCP alone is not end-to-end.
questions.hint: Ordering needs sequence handling or one ordered channel.

questions.topic: A batching window and the latency it buys with
questions.learningObjective: Explain the latency trade-off of a batching window
questions.stem: A 50ms batching window for plan updates trades what for throughput?

options.text: Up to 50ms of added latency per update

questions.explanation: A batch window delays each update by up to the window. Throughput rises but latency increases.
questions.hint: Window adds up to window latency.

questions.topic: A delta sync and the baseline it is measured from
questions.learningObjective: Define the baseline for a delta sync
questions.stem: A delta sync returns changes since timestamp T; what must T represent?

options.misconception: would skip changes since last sync

options.text: The client's last successful sync point, not the server's current time

questions.explanation: The baseline must be the client's last sync point. Using current time skips changes.

questions.topic: How long a tombstone has to be kept
questions.learningObjective: Determine tombstone retention duration
questions.stem: How long must a tombstone be kept for a deleted plan?

answer.exemplar: It must be kept at least as long as the oldest client that has not synced could still hold a stale copy, so that client can learn of the deletion.

questions.explanation: Tombstones must outlive the slowest client's stale state. Shorter retention hides deletions.

questions.topic: A client clock four minutes fast and an empty delta set
questions.learningObjective: Diagnose an empty delta caused by clock skew
questions.stem: A client clock is four minutes fast and its delta sync returns nothing; why?

options.text: The client asks for changes after its fast future timestamp, skipping recent ones

questions.explanation: A fast clock makes the baseline future, so recent changes are skipped. The server still responds successfully.

questions.topic: Choosing an invalidation strategy for a cache
questions.learningObjective: Choose a cache invalidation strategy
questions.stem: Plan updates are frequent and consistency matters; which invalidation strategy fits?

options.misconception: reads do not know about writes

questions.explanation: Write-through invalidation keeps cache consistent with writes. TTL-only or read-time invalidation risks staleness.

questions.topic: A subscription that is registered twice and torn down once
questions.learningObjective: Prevent a leaked subscription from double registration
questions.stem: A component mounts twice and registers two subscriptions but unmounts once; what leaks?

options.text: Nothing; the second registration overwrites the first
One subscription remains active and fires stale updates

questions.explanation: Double registration with single teardown leaks one subscription. Overwrite is not automatic.
questions.hint: Each registration needs a matching teardown.

questions.topic: A polling interval chosen without counting the cost
questions.learningObjective: Account for polling cost when choosing an interval
questions.stem: A 1-second poll interval for 10,000 clients; what is the main problem?

options.text: Request volume overwhelms the server and wastes battery

questions.explanation: High-frequency polling scales poorly and drains clients. Staleness is not the issue at 1 second.
questions.hint: Polling cost grows with clients times frequency.

questions.topic: A long poll and the connections it holds open
questions.learningObjective: Explain the connection cost of long polling
questions.stem: Why does long polling strain a server with many clients?

answer.exemplar: Each client holds an open connection waiting for an event, so connection count and memory grow with clients even when no data flows.

questions.explanation: Long polling ties up connections per client. The cost is connection state, not data transfer.

questions.topic: Server authoritative state and a body the client filled in
questions.learningObjective: Reject client-authored fields in server state
questions.stem: A client sends a plan with a server-computed score field; what should the server do?

options.text: Ignore or reject the client's score and recompute it
Return the score to the client unchanged

questions.explanation: Server-authoritative fields must be recomputed server-side. Trusting client input risks forgery.

questions.topic: A merge rule and the edit it discards without record
questions.learningObjective: Identify a merge rule that silently drops an edit
questions.stem: A last-write-wins merge discards an earlier edit without logging; what is lost?

options.text: Nothing, because LWW always keeps the best edit
The earlier edit's content and any audit trail of it

questions.explanation: Last-write-wins keeps only the latest edit and drops prior content and history. It does not pick the best edit.
questions.hint: LWW keeps only the latest edit.

questions.topic: Choosing a transport for updates
questions.learningObjective: Choose a transport given update direction and frequency
questions.stem: Frequent bidirectional plan updates between client and server; which transport fits?

options.text: WebSocket, because it supports full-duplex over one connection

questions.explanation: WebSockets provide full-duplex for frequent bidirectional updates. SSE and polling are inferior here.

questions.topic: A consistency claim contradicted by the service's own merge rule
questions.learningObjective: Spot a contradiction between a consistency claim and merge rule
questions.stem: A service claims strong consistency but uses last-write-wins; what contradicts?

options.misconception: cache is unrelated to consistency model

options.text: LWW can silently drop concurrent edits, violating strong consistency

questions.explanation: Last-write-wins loses concurrent edits, so strong consistency is not provided. LWW is not strongly consistent.

questions.topic: A cache entry that no write ever cleared
questions.learningObjective: Explain a stale cache entry never invalidated
questions.stem: A plan's cached value never updates after edits; what is likely missing?

answer.exemplar: The update path never invalidates or refreshes the cache entry, so reads keep returning the old cached value forever.

questions.explanation: Without invalidation on write, the cache stays stale. TTL or write-through would fix it.

questions.topic: A handler registered again by a second mount
questions.learningObjective: Avoid duplicate handler registration on remount
questions.stem: A component remounts and registers its event handler again; what happens?

options.text: The second registration replaces the first
The handler fires twice per event until one registration is removed

questions.explanation: Duplicate registrations both fire. Cleanup on unmount prevents accumulation.

questions.topic: What a document shape permits that a table of columns cannot
questions.learningObjective: Recognize when a document shape complicates joins
questions.stem: When is a document shape a poor fit?

options.text: When many-to-many relationships must be queried efficiently

questions.explanation: Documents struggle with efficient many-to-many queries. Optionality and hierarchy suit documents.

questions.topic: The write cost an index adds
questions.learningObjective: Measure write amplification from indexes
questions.stem: With 5 indexes on plans, one insert updates how many structures?

options.text: Six: the table plus five indexes

questions.explanation: An insert writes the base table and every index. Lazy or buffered myths are false.

questions.topic: Reading the three words a plan uses to describe its work
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish index scan from index-only scan
questions.stem: What is the difference between an index scan and an index-only scan?

answer.exemplar: An index scan uses the index to find rows but fetches columns from the table, while an index-only scan returns all needed columns from the index itself.

questions.explanation: Index-only avoids table fetches. Index scan still needs the table for columns.

questions.topic: A server-sent event and the one direction it allows
questions.learningObjective: Send client input when using SSE
questions.stem: A client needs to send a plan update while receiving SSE updates; what must it do?

options.text: Embed the update in a comment

options.misconception: SSE is read-only for the client

options.text: Issue a separate HTTP request for the update

questions.explanation: SSE carries no client-to-server channel, so updates need a separate request. EventSource has no send method.
questions.hint: SSE has no client send channel.

questions.topic: A socket that closes and the handshake that reopens it
questions.learningObjective: Implement reconnection with backoff for a WebSocket
questions.stem: How should a client reopen a dropped WebSocket robustly?

options.text: Spin in a tight loop reconnecting
Retry the upgrade handshake with exponential backoff
Wait for the user to refresh

questions.explanation: Backoff reconnection is robust and polite. Tight loops harm the server; manual refresh is poor UX.

questions.topic: What actually delivers an ordering guarantee
questions.learningObjective: Add sequence numbers to guarantee order across reconnects
questions.stem: How can the planning feed guarantee order across reconnects?

answer.exemplar: Include a monotonic sequence number in each event and have the client reorder or request replay from the last seen sequence on reconnect.

questions.explanation: Sequence numbers enable reordering and replay. Relying on transport order alone breaks across reconnects.

questions.topic: A batching window and the latency it buys with
questions.learningObjective: Choose a batching window given latency budget
questions.stem: The planning UI requires updates within 100ms; what max batch window is acceptable?

options.text: Zero, because batching is never allowed
Any window, because batching is always better
At most 100ms, and less if processing adds delay

questions.explanation: The window must fit the latency budget including processing. Any window or zero are extremes.
questions.hint: Window plus processing must fit budget.

questions.topic: A delta sync and the baseline it is measured from
questions.learningObjective: Handle a missing baseline on first sync
questions.stem: On first sync a client has no baseline; what should the server send?

options.misconception: first sync has no prior baseline

options.text: The full current state, then record the new baseline

questions.explanation: First sync needs a full snapshot and a new baseline. Empty or epoch deltas are wrong.

questions.topic: How long a tombstone has to be kept
questions.learningObjective: Garbage-collect tombstones safely
questions.stem: Tombstones are garbage-collected too early; what breaks?

options.text: The server runs out of memory
A late-syncing client never learns of the deletion

questions.explanation: Early GC hides deletions from late clients. Memory is not the issue.
questions.hint: Late clients miss deletions if GC is early.

questions.topic: A client clock four minutes fast and an empty delta set
questions.learningObjective: Mitigate clock skew in delta sync
questions.stem: How can delta sync be made robust to client clock skew?

answer.exemplar: Use server-issued cursors or sequence numbers instead of client timestamps, so the baseline is authoritative and skew cannot skip changes.

questions.explanation: Server-issued cursors remove client clock dependence. Client timestamps invite skew.

questions.topic: Choosing an invalidation strategy for a cache
questions.learningObjective: Pick invalidation for a read-heavy cache
questions.stem: A read-heavy plan cache rarely updated; which invalidation strategy is cheapest?

options.text: TTL with a moderate expiry plus write-through on the rare updates

questions.explanation: TTL plus write-through on updates balances cost and freshness. Read-time or excessive invalidation wastes work.

questions.topic: A subscription that is registered twice and torn down once
questions.learningObjective: Fix double registration with a cleanup guard
questions.stem: How to prevent the subscription leak on remount?

options.text: Return a cleanup function that unsubscribes on unmount

questions.explanation: A cleanup function ensures each registration is undone. Disabling strict mode or flags are workarounds.

questions.topic: A polling interval chosen without counting the cost
questions.learningObjective: Compute polling load from interval and clients
questions.stem: 10,000 clients polling every 5 seconds produce how many requests per minute?

options.misconception: off by a factor of ten

questions.explanation: 10,000 clients times 12 requests per minute equals 120,000. The other values misconvert.

questions.topic: A long poll and the connections it holds open
questions.learningObjective: Replace long polling with SSE or WebSockets
questions.stem: Long polling holds too many connections; what is a better alternative?

options.text: SSE for server-push or WebSockets for bidirectional

questions.explanation: SSE or WebSockets reduce connection churn. Shorter timeouts or more servers are workarounds.

questions.topic: Server authoritative state and a body the client filled in
questions.learningObjective: Validate a plan body against server rules
questions.stem: How should the server handle a client-submitted plan with an invalid status value?

answer.exemplar: Reject the request with a validation error listing the allowed statuses, rather than silently coercing or storing the invalid value.

questions.explanation: Rejecting with a clear error preserves integrity. Coercing hides bad input.
questions.hint: Reject invalid values with a clear error.

questions.topic: A merge rule and the edit it discards without record
questions.learningObjective: Choose a merge rule that preserves concurrent edits
questions.stem: Which merge rule preserves concurrent edits instead of dropping one?

options.text: Three-way merge or CRDT that combines both changes

questions.explanation: Three-way merge or CRDTs combine concurrent changes. LWW and first-write-wins drop one side.
questions.hint: Combine changes, do not pick one.

questions.topic: Choosing a transport for updates
questions.learningObjective: Choose SSE for one-way server push
questions.stem: One-way live plan notifications from server to browser; which transport is simplest?
questions.explanation: SSE is the simplest one-way push. WebSockets and polling are heavier.
questions.hint: SSE is simplest for one-way push.

questions.topic: A consistency claim contradicted by the service's own merge rule
questions.learningObjective: Align consistency claims with implementation
questions.stem: How to make a strong consistency claim credible?

options.text: Use consensus or serializable transactions and document them
Use last-write-wins with a faster clock

questions.explanation: Credible strong consistency needs consensus or serializable transactions. Marketing or TTL changes do not help.

questions.topic: A cache entry that no write ever cleared
questions.learningObjective: Add write-through invalidation to a cache
questions.stem: The plan cache never clears on update; what minimal fix?

options.text: Lower the TTL to one second
Invalidate or update the cache entry in the write path

questions.explanation: Invalidating in the write path fixes staleness precisely. Restarting or short TTLs are imprecise.

questions.topic: A handler registered again by a second mount
questions.learningObjective: Use a stable handler reference to avoid duplicate registration
questions.stem: How can a component avoid registering a handler twice on remount?

answer.exemplar: Use a stable callback reference and register once in an effect with a cleanup, so remount runs cleanup before re-registering.

questions.explanation: Cleanup plus stable references prevent duplicate registration. Global flags are fragile.
questions.hint: Register in an effect with cleanup.

questions.topic: What a document shape permits that a table of columns cannot
questions.learningObjective: Store an array of steps in one document
questions.stem: A plan with an ordered list of steps fits which shape better?

options.text: A single column of comma-joined text
A document with an embedded steps array

questions.explanation: An embedded array preserves order and structure. Comma text or blobs lose queryability.

questions.topic: The write cost an index adds
questions.learningObjective: Decide whether an index is worth its write cost
questions.stem: A rarely queried but heavily written plans table; should you add a secondary index?

options.text: Always yes, indexes are always beneficial
Probably not, unless the read benefit exceeds write cost

questions.explanation: Indexes trade write cost for read benefit. Always-yes or never are extremes.
questions.hint: Weigh read benefit against write cost.

questions.topic: Reading the three words a plan uses to describe its work
questions.learningObjective: Read a nested loop join in a plan
questions.stem: A plan shows Nested Loop with an index seek on the inner side; what does that imply?

options.text: For each outer row, the inner relation is probed via the index

questions.explanation: Nested loop probes the inner relation per outer row using the index. Full scans describe other joins.
questions.hint: Inner is probed per outer row.

questions.topic: A server-sent event and the one direction it allows
questions.learningObjective: Handle SSE reconnection and last-event-id
questions.stem: After an SSE disconnect, how does the client resume without gaps?

options.text: Send Last-Event-ID on reconnect so the server replays missed events

questions.explanation: Last-Event-ID enables replay of missed events. Reconnecting bare loses them.

questions.topic: A socket that closes and the handshake that reopens it
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish close codes and reasons
questions.stem: Why should a WebSocket close handler inspect the close code?

answer.exemplar: The code distinguishes normal closure from errors, so the client can decide whether to reconnect or surface a failure.

questions.explanation: Close codes guide reconnection decisions. Ignoring them treats all closes the same.

questions.topic: What actually delivers an ordering guarantee
questions.learningObjective: Detect out-of-order delivery in a stream
questions.stem: How can the client detect out-of-order events in a stream?

options.text: Check that each sequence number is exactly one greater than the last

questions.explanation: Monotonic sequence numbers reveal gaps or reordering. Timestamps and sizes are unreliable.

questions.topic: A batching window and the latency it buys with
questions.learningObjective: Flush a batch early on a high-priority update
questions.stem: A high-priority plan update arrives mid-batch; what should the system do?

options.text: Send it out of band without batching
Wait for the window to expire
Flush the current batch immediately, then start a new one

questions.explanation: Flushing preserves batching while prioritizing urgent data. Waiting or dropping is wrong.

questions.topic: A delta sync and the baseline it is measured from
questions.learningObjective: Version the baseline to detect stale clients
questions.stem: Why should a delta baseline include a version or generation?

options.text: To detect when the client's baseline is too old to diff against

questions.explanation: A versioned baseline lets the server detect unsupportable old baselines. It is not for encryption or compression.

questions.topic: How long a tombstone has to be kept
questions.learningObjective: Measure the oldest client sync age
questions.stem: How should the system determine tombstone retention duration?

answer.exemplar: Track the oldest last-sync timestamp among active clients and retain tombstones at least that long plus a safety margin.

questions.explanation: Retention must cover the slowest client. A fixed short duration risks missing deletions.
questions.hint: Retain based on oldest client sync.

questions.topic: A client clock four minutes fast and an empty delta set
questions.learningObjective: Detect clock skew from an empty delta
questions.stem: A client gets empty deltas repeatedly while others get updates; what should the server check?

options.text: Whether the plan table is empty
Whether the client's baseline timestamp is in the future

questions.explanation: A future baseline from clock skew skips all changes. Other causes are inconsistent with others receiving updates.

questions.topic: Choosing an invalidation strategy for a cache
questions.learningObjective: Invalidate cache on related entity changes
questions.stem: A plan cache must invalidate when its owner member changes; how?

options.text: Invalidate plan entries keyed by that member on member update

questions.explanation: Targeted invalidation on member update keeps related plan caches fresh. Global or none are extremes.

questions.topic: A subscription that is registered twice and torn down once
questions.learningObjective: Use a ref count for shared subscriptions
questions.stem: Multiple components share one subscription; how to manage its lifetime?

options.text: Create a new subscription per component
Reference count registrations and teardown only at zero

questions.explanation: Reference counting shares one subscription safely. Per-component or never-teardown are wasteful or leaky.

questions.topic: A polling interval chosen without counting the cost
questions.learningObjective: Replace polling with push where possible
questions.stem: When should polling be replaced by push?

answer.exemplar: Replace polling with push when updates are frequent or latency matters, since push avoids repeated requests and reduces server load.

questions.explanation: Push suits frequent or latency-sensitive updates. Polling wastes requests when events are sparse but latency-sensitive.
questions.hint: Push for frequent or urgent updates.

questions.topic: A long poll and the connections it holds open
questions.learningObjective: Limit long-poll connection duration
questions.stem: How to cap the cost of long polling per client?

options.text: Set a maximum wait time then require reconnect

questions.explanation: A max wait bounds connection lifetime. Indefinite holds exhaust resources.

questions.topic: Server authoritative state and a body the client filled in
questions.learningObjective: Strip client-only fields on the server
questions.stem: A client sends display-only fields in a plan body; what should the server do?

options.text: Return them in the response only
Ignore or strip them, since they are not server state

questions.explanation: Display-only fields should not become server state. Storing them risks forgery; rejecting is excessive.

questions.topic: A merge rule and the edit it discards without record
questions.learningObjective: Log discarded edits for audit
questions.stem: When a merge discards an edit, what should be recorded?

options.text: The discarded edit, its author, and the reason

questions.explanation: Auditing discarded edits preserves traceability. Storing nothing or only final values loses history.

questions.topic: Choosing a transport for updates
questions.learningObjective: Fallback from WebSocket to polling
questions.stem: A WebSocket connection fails repeatedly; what is a reasonable fallback?

options.text: Retry the socket in a tight loop
Fall back to SSE or polling with backoff

questions.explanation: Falling back to SSE or polling preserves functionality. Giving up or tight-loop retry is poor.
questions.hint: Fall back to SSE or polling.

questions.topic: A consistency claim contradicted by the service's own merge rule
questions.learningObjective: Downgrade a consistency claim to match implementation
questions.stem: If the service uses LWW, what consistency claim can it honestly make?

answer.exemplar: It can claim eventual consistency, since LWW converges to the latest write but may drop concurrent edits in the meantime.

questions.explanation: LWW provides eventual consistency at best. Strong consistency would be dishonest.

questions.topic: A cache entry that no write ever cleared
questions.learningObjective: Test cache invalidation on write
questions.stem: How to test that a cache invalidates on write?

options.text: Write a new value, then read and assert the new value appears

questions.explanation: Writing then reading verifies invalidation. Reading twice or checking TTL tests other things.
questions.hint: Write then read to verify invalidation.

questions.topic: A handler registered again by a second mount
questions.learningObjective: Avoid duplicate handlers with a single registration point
questions.stem: Best way to ensure a global handler is registered only once?

options.text: Register in a module-level singleton with a guard flag

questions.explanation: A singleton with a guard ensures one registration. Per-component or render-time registration duplicates.
